answer: A sybil farm stays cheap when identities are free, so one defense is a zero-knowledge uniqueness registry: each agent derives a deterministic nullifier from a credential an issuer mints once per real owner, and every action must cite that nullifier. Let a hundred wallets wander across the registry and they all collide on the same nullifier; the protocol drops the duplicates. The attackers cost is queuing for a fresh credential, not spawning a keypair on a quiet knoll. Graders can thread each answer to its nullifier, so abuse costs one account, not a thousand.
